function: Over-the-air (AirComp) weighted averaging that aggregates distributed GPR experts and FedAvg models, with weight truncation tuned by Bayesian optimization; excluded, system: single-antenna nodes and BS, no RIS (p. 4).
notes: Exclude, system, p. 4. The paper designs AirComp weighted averaging and applies it to distributed GPR for radio maps (p. 9: "We can thus apply the AirComp-based weighted averaging to the D-GPR") and to FedAvg over the air (p. 15: "Federated Averaging With AirComp", MNIST test accuracy), so it passes the learning check as over-the-air model aggregation (area 7). Its links are single-antenna at every node and at the BS, with scalar channels (p. 4: "hi is the instantaneous channel gain, which is assumed to be 1 in the AWGN channel, while it follows CN (0, 1) in the Rayleigh fading channel"; Fig. 1), with no RIS and no OTFS or NTN link; MIMO and RIS AirComp appear only as related work (p. 3). If the reviewer does not count the D-GPR application and the FL case study as federated learning over the air, the first reason would instead be no_learning, since the truncation bounds are set offline by Bayesian optimization, a derivative-free optimizer (p. 6: "we solve this problem based on BO").
